raw_case_text:
A 48-year-old male with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia in partial remission receiving inpatient chemotherapy experienced left eye progressive vision loss, tearing, and redness for three days. On ophthalmological consultation, the left eye had a visual acuity of counting fingers at 1 foot with an afferent pupillary defect. Examination revealed 4+ cell and flare in the anterior chamber with 2mm hypopyon and dense vitreous haze in the posterior pole. Given the concern for endogenous endophthalmitis in an immunocompromised patient, a diagnostic pars plana vitrectomy was performed and a vitreous biopsy was obtained. Intravitreal antibiotics and antifungals were injected through the trocars. Intraoperatively, a pink nonpigmented 2 x 3 x 2mm (W x L x H) elevation was noted on the mid-peripheral superonasal retina. Given this lesion and the patient's declining mental status, imaging and cerebrospinal fluid sampling were performed. MRI brain illustrated rim-enhancing lesions with diffusion restriction in the right peritrigonal and left corona radiata (Figure 1) while orbital sections showed circumferential smooth enhancement in the left globe and optic nerve sheath (Figures 2 and 3). Cerebrospinal fluid removed from the right frontal ventricular reservoir through which the patient was receiving intrathecal chemotherapy showed no bacterial or fungal growth.
Despite systemic use of antibiotics and antifungal medications, the patient's mental status over the next several days declined to the point where he could no longer follow commands. Repeat MRI brain 10 days later showed increasing sizes of the rim-enhancing lesions. Vision became "no light perception (NLP)," inferior retinal detachment was noted on exam, and the vitreous biopsy had still not grown any organisms. Both culture-negative endophthalmitis and uveitis masquerade syndromes such as intraocular malignancy still remained real life-threatening possibilities. Given the systemic risk of a bacteremia or malignancy, the ophthalmology team decided to proceed with a transvitreal retinochoroidal biopsy. Septate filamentous fungi with acute angle branching characteristic of Aspergillus fumigatus were noted on retinochoroidal biopsy (Figure 4(a)). The patient was subsequently started on systemic voriconazole and amphotericin B. Two weeks later, culture from the initial vitrectomy demonstrated Aspergillus fumigatus (Figure 4(b)). Pathology from the brain tissue that was biopsied by neurosurgery demonstrated organisms morphologically consistent with Aspergillus as well (Figure 4(c)). Flow cytometry to rule out intraocular malignancy demonstrated an immunophenotypically normal cell population and cytology done on the vitreous biopsy did not show malignant cells. The patient was ultimately discharged from the hospital to a rehabilitation facility where he was informed that he would likely need enucleation of the left eye as an outpatient.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 48-year-old male with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia receiving inpatient chemotherapy presented with a 3-day history of progressive left eye vision loss, tearing, and redness, accompanied by declining mental status.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: While hospitalized for chemotherapy for B-cell ALL in partial remission, the patient developed 3 days of progressive left visual loss, epiphora, and conjunctival redness. Diagnostic pars plana vitrectomy with intravitreal antimicrobials was performed, but over the ensuing 10 days his left vision deteriorated to no light perception with an inferior retinal detachment while his mental status progressively declined until he could no longer follow commands.
subjective.past_medical_history: B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) in partial remission receiving systemic and intrathecal chemotherapy via a right frontal ventricular reservoir.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for progressive left eye vision loss (to NLP), tearing, ocular redness, and progressive mental status decline.

objective.physical_examination: Initial left eye exam showed visual acuity of counting fingers at 1 foot, a relative afferent pupillary defect, 4+ anterior chamber cells and flare with a 2-mm hypopyon, dense posterior vitreous haze, and an intraoperative 2 x 3 x 2 mm pink nonpigmented mid-peripheral superonasal retinal mass. Over 10 days, left vision declined to no light perception (NLP) with an inferior retinal detachment, and neurological status deteriorated to inability to follow commands.
objective.routine_investigations: CSF sampled from the right frontal ventricular reservoir showed no bacterial or fungal growth.
objective.advanced_workup: Brain and orbital MRI demonstrated diffusion-restricting rim-enhancing cerebral abscesses in the right peritrigonal white matter and left corona radiata (which enlarged on day 10 repeat MRI) along with circumferential enhancement of the left globe and optic nerve sheath. Vitreous biopsy cytology and flow cytometry excluded intraocular leukemic infiltration. Because initial vitreous cultures remained negative at day 10, a transvitreal retinochoroidal biopsy was performed, revealing acute-angle branching septate filamentous hyphae characteristic of Aspergillus fumigatus; initial vitrectomy culture subsequently grew Aspergillus fumigatus at 2 weeks, and neurosurgical brain biopsy pathology also confirmed Aspergillus hyphae.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Proven disseminated invasive aspergillosis (Aspergillus fumigatus) presenting with endogenous left eye retinochoroiditis/endophthalmitis and multifocal cerebral abscesses in an immunocompromised patient with B-cell ALL, definitively confirmed by transvitreal retinochoroidal biopsy histopathology, vitrectomy fungal culture, and neurosurgical brain biopsy pathology (with leukemic masquerade syndrome ruled out by flow cytometry and cytology). Treated with diagnostic vitrectomy, intravitreal antimicrobials, and systemic combination voriconazole plus amphotericin B, stabilizing the patient for discharge to a rehabilitation facility with planned outpatient enucleation of the blind left eye.
